source.original_title: 05/13/2026 - Mao Sal & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
source.display_title: 05/13/2026 - Mao Sal & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Follow Up

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Rep: 'i know you spoke with kim he kind of gave me like a little bit of a head start on you'. The prospect refers to her too, rendered by the transcriber as 'I'm not sure Tim told you the whole story'.

prospect.name: Moath Abdullah ALOBEID
prospect.family_status: Married; wife is 12 years younger than him and is naturally slim with little interest in training. No children yet — 'I will have kids hopefully one day'.
prospect.training_background: Started training at university in the United States and has been on and off ever since — never more than six months off, but typically drops out around the two-month mark once he starts seeing progress. Moved from cardio-led programmes to compound barbell work only: deadlift, squat, bench, overhead press, pull-ups, no isolation. Gained significant weight during COVID working from home. Found steel clubs during Ramadan (March/April) and kettlebells about three to four weeks before the call after seeing Trevor's reels. Uses a 10 kg bell. Long-standing intermittent faster since 2012/2013, with occasional 24, 48 and 72-hour fasts; has done two vegetarian stints which he blames for much of his weight gain. Has never had a coach of any kind.
prospect.medical: Self-reported shoulder problem: 'when I move my hands, and there's always a click in my shoulder, I have a rotated cup, so I try to fix it with, like, stretching'. Postural issue he calls 'the duck posture'. Already hurt his arm attempting a kettlebell movement — 'i hurt my arm here when i tried it'. Persistent fear of acute injury under the bell: 'I'm gonna snap something, you know, like, when I hold it up and I feel like something's gonna snap all of a sudden.' Overweight since COVID. Stiffness he says he hates, and a fear of injuring himself on a big step down. No clinician, diagnosis, imaging or treatment mentioned anywhere on the call.

signals: Explicitly lost ground in a hard season and wants the former version back: 'I've been the healthy one in the past. For the longest time, until COVID hit, I got fatter'
Carries visible regret about a specific period: 'I blame it, all the overweight I am in, I blame it in that period'
Approaching a milestone age with a stated ageing motive: 'especially I'm reaching 40, I want to be healthy, want to age well'
A decade of restarts rather than a plateau at a high level: 'I get into it maybe two months into the training, and then I drop out'
Not the optimizer — he is not moving good to great, he is trying to recover a baseline he used to hold

goals.text: Be healthy and age well as he approaches 40 — the primary stated driver
Keep up with a wife who is 12 years younger than him
Get his kettlebell form right so he stops feeling he is about to snap something
Finally find consistency after a decade of two-month cycles, and build enough momentum that he knows how to get back in when he inevitably falls off
Lose the weight gained during COVID and get lean — explicitly not for looks alone
Get rid of the stiffness he lives in and move without fear of injury on a big step down
Train inside his existing life rather than reorganising his life around training — 15 minutes at home, even late at night, without the commute
Be one of the ripped older men he sees on social media

pains.text: Cannot sustain training — drops out roughly two months in, every time, for a decade
Gym logistics have become incompatible with married life: changing, driving, traffic, getting home late
Shoulder clicks and a self-described rotator cuff problem; already hurt his arm attempting a kettlebell movement
Fear of acute injury under the bell — feels something will snap when he holds it overhead
Knows he is doing the movements wrong and gets confused watching Trevor's videos, then stops: 'it just gets confusing. And then I stop and don't do it.'
Stiffness he hates, plus a postural problem he calls the duck posture
Binge eating pattern layered on top of long fasts, which drove the COVID weight gain
Gym training became boring, which is the proximate cause of each dropout
Two vegetarian attempts backfired and added weight while he believed he was being healthy

objections.raw_quote: to be honest, I didn't think it's going to be that high, but it is a commitment, and he's going to give me my time, so he's an expert, I'm sure that costs some money
objections.rep_response: Asked what was holding him back and whether it was the money up front, then asked a value-projection question — 'let's say you did six months, and in six months' time you got everything you wanted out of it, would it be worth the money?' — to which the prospect said yes. Then used a quality frame, 'if you want the best, you've got to pay for the best', and pivoted to payment plans. No financial-picture questions were asked at any point.

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, I feel it's too much. Because I have less expectations, that's why it's not. I'm not saying that it actually should cost less, because at his time and his expertise, he can value that better, not me to value him. But this is not what I expected.
objections.rep_response: Conceded the point ('Sometimes, I guess, it depends, really'), acknowledged cheaper alternatives exist — 'I'm sure there's somebody who would do it for 2k' — then offered instalments and subsequently walked the price down through the three-month and one-month terms.

objections.raw_quote: why I'm saying that, because I want to first check if I can withdraw some of my, because I have this monthly thing that I pay off. And if I can see if I can withdraw from that for this month or not.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it and moved to exchange WhatsApp numbers. No attempt to structure a start date around the withdrawal, no deposit proposed, no timeline agreed.

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, I would need to get back to you on that. That's okay. Let me just think about it. So just to check my options.
objections.rep_response: Let it stand and recapped the payment options instead of running the play. The prospect then generated his own downward options — three months, then one month — and the rep supplied prices for both.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Two options given live for the six-month term. Option 1: 50% down ($3,000 / SAR 11,000) with the remaining 50% due within 90 days — 'as long as the other 11K is done within three months, you basically pay for the first three months and then you just pay the rest in 90 days.' Option 2: monthly at $1,200/month, explicitly priced at a premium — 'if you do monthly, we add a little bit on, so it would be 4,500 real a month' — which over six months totals $7,200 against a $6,000 list price. The rep recommended option 1: 'if you just do the 3K down and then 3K in three months, it's a lot better.'
offer.guarantee_mentioned: 'we guarantee you results. We guarantee you that in six months or in 12 months time, that you'll put on eight kilos, in six months, you'll put on eight kilos of weight on every kettlebell movement. And if you put on eight kilos of weight in every kettlebell movement, your body will reflect that.' No conditions, remedy, refund term or qualifying criteria were stated.

prospect_financials.note: Only disclosure was an existing monthly financial commitment he might be able to draw against: 'I have this monthly thing that I pay off. And if I can see if I can withdraw from that for this month or not.' He also revealed his price expectation was roughly SAR 8,000 (~$2,000) for six months. No cash-on-hand, surplus, credit or investment questions were asked.

evidence: No payment taken and no payment link sent — the rep explicitly declined to send one: 'we have to be on a call for me to onboard you'
Strong buying signal left on the table: the prospect asked 'If you can send me the links, or do we have to do it now?' at 00:44:06 and the call ended 3 minutes later with nothing booked
Verbal lean toward the one-month term but not an agreement: 'yeah i actually might do them one month'
Blocking condition is unresolved cash access: 'I want to first check if I can withdraw some of my... monthly thing that I pay off'
No follow-up call was scheduled — rep offered 9pm the same evening, prospect deflected to 'I'll email you', and it settled on an open-ended WhatsApp exchange

Counter-evidence toward eventual close: high engagement across 48 minutes, all three pillars landed enthusiastically, and the prospect volunteered his real phone number after admitting the one on his application was fake
outcome.next_step: Rep to message on WhatsApp (+966 56 999 7769); prospect to check whether he can withdraw from an existing monthly financial product, then arrange a further call to be onboarded. No date, no time, no deposit.

notable.note: Two things a manager needs to see. First, the rep explicitly declined to run discovery — 'thank you for telling me pretty much everything I needed to know, all the context, it makes my job a lot easier than trying to ask a million different questions' — and as a result never asked occupation, income, sleep, energy, or a single goals-phase question. The prospect's deepest driver, turning 40 with a wife 12 years younger, was handed over unprompted and answered with 'Yeah, congratulations.' Second, on hesitation the price walked from $6,000 to $4,000 to $1,200 in about eight minutes, and a specific unconditional performance guarantee was made — eight kilos added to every kettlebell movement in six months — with no terms attached. The prospect also disclosed a clicking shoulder and rotator cuff issue and an arm he had already hurt on a kettlebell, and nobody asked whether a clinician had looked at it.

quality.notes: Severe throughout. The entire opening block to 00:01:05 is attributed to the rep but contains both sides. From 00:10:44 to 00:13:26 the labels invert repeatedly — 'Here's what I'm curious about' and 'What's kind of going on there?' are the rep, while 'What weight do you use?' at 00:11:43 is the rep and '10 kilos' is the prospect. The critical pricing block at 00:34:06 is labelled 'Moath Abdullah ALOBEID' but contains the rep quoting '6k US' and '9k US'. The one-month price at 00:42:45 is similarly inverted. Every price attribution in this file needs to be read from content, not labels.
